_note: Batch 1 draft (author pass, pre-review). 5 sci-fi theme tag sets. Requirements: sci-fi, artifacts, alien civilizations (need NOT be fallen). Resource tie-ins welcome but not mandatory for all. Psychic OPTIONAL (per Sam) — varied here. Breadth is the goal: each should produce worlds that don't feel like siblings of the others or of the original fallen-civ/psychic theme (#0).

sets.title: The Ones Still Watching
sets.hook: The aliens are alive, ancient, and vetting humanity in real time. They lend a trickle of technology as a test; the artifacts that matter are the ones they WON'T give you — sealed caches you must locate and prove worthy to open, every unlock raising the stakes of the relationship.
sets.artifact_flavor: Two tiers: lent gifts whose correct use is a vetting test, and withheld caches of high-value technology you must hunt down and earn the right to open — misuse of a gift can lock a cache forever or read as an act of war.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: Aliens are PRESENT, reactive, and the gatekeepers of the hunt — you earn artifacts by proving trustworthy, not by looting a tomb. The drama is reading intent across an unbridgeable gap, not piecing together a fall.

sets.title: The Green Cathedral
sets.hook: The 'civilization' is one vast living organism that covers a world and thinks as a single mind; its artifacts are grown, not built, and to use them is to be slowly colonized — your thoughts joining a chorus that already considers you part of itself.
sets.artifact_flavor: Bio-relics — seeds, spores, grown tools, symbiotes — that grant power while rewriting the user and patching them into the organism's shared awareness; the resource IS the organism's living tissue, and harvesting it is felt by the whole.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: Organic, intimate, transformation-horror with an OVERT hive-mind psychic register. Resource exploitation is literally harvesting a living mind's body — but the horror is becoming/joining, not extinction.

sets.title: The Patient Engine
sets.hook: A self-replicating machine civilization went quiet ten thousand years ago, leaving the galaxy littered with its still-running cores. Each core hoards power and a different fragment of a vast, half-finished intent; collecting and running them is the resource race — and the question of whether the silence is death or patience.
sets.artifact_flavor: Functional machine cores, each encoding a DIFFERENT shard of a single galaxy-spanning purpose; they are simultaneously the power/energy economy you exploit and the prize you hunt — but every core you wake votes on what the whole intends to do next.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: Cold, logical, recursive dread; no biology, no psychic. The cores ARE the resource economy (high centrality), and the mystery is reconstructing a divergent machine INTENT, not a cause-of-death.

sets.title: Objects Out of Order
sets.hook: An alien civilization waged war through time itself, and whether it is alive or dead is not yet settled — the conflict is still resolving. Its artifacts arrive out of sequence: effects before causes, relics that remember a future. Reconstructing the order means later finds rewrite what the earlier ones meant.
sets.artifact_flavor: Anachronisms — an object older than its maker, a relic that remembers a future, a tool whose function changes once you find the one that 'caused' it; each new find retro-edits the meaning of everything collected so far.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: The mystery is non-linear: clues arrive out of order, contradict, and retroactively rewrite each other, and the civilization's very fate is UNDECIDED rather than excavated. Resource element deliberately absent — this is a causality puzzle, not a dig.

sets.title: We Were the Aliens
sets.hook: The 'alien' ruins fit human hands too well. As the colonists dig, the artifacts — memory-cores, sealed vaults, edited star-charts, monuments with names scratched out — reveal that they are the descendants of the civilization they're excavating, and that their ancestors engineered the great forgetting on purpose. The world-gen decides, per world, WHAT was worth burying.
sets.artifact_flavor: A varied substrate of self-referential relics — memory-cores, sealed bio-vaults, redacted star-charts, defaced monuments, encrypted wills — each a recovered piece of the colony's own redacted history, no two worlds hiding the same secret.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: The 'alien' civilization turns out to be us. The mystery is introspective — who are we and what did we choose to bury — rather than xeno-archaeology of a stranger; resources are incidental to the reckoning.
